monthly_review.summary: This month shows a slight pacing slowdown and increased HR zone intensity compared to last month, with notable gains in aerobic efficiency and cadence consistency — reflecting improved neuromuscular coordination despite reduced volume at higher intensities.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite a slower average pace (+8 sec/km), aerobic training effect increased by +0.2 and aerobic efficiency improved (+0.07 km/h per bpm), indicating more effective physiological adaptation per unit of effort.

goal_tracker.message: You need 0.5 more km across up to 3 remaining sessions to match last month’s distance — e.g., add 0.2 km to one run and 0.3 km to another, or complete a single 0.5 km easy jog before month-end.

insights.title: Improved efficiency despite slower pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.28 to 13.35 km/h per bpm — meaning you’re moving farther per heartbeat, even as avg pace slowed from 534 to 542 sec/km. This signals better cardiovascular economy, likely supported by the 23% Z1 time this month (vs 4% last month).

insights.title: Strategic shift toward lower- and higher-intensity work
insights.body: Z1 time jumped from 4% to 23%, while Z3 dropped from 36% to 26% and Z4 rose from 12% to 17%. This reflects intentional recovery and threshold work — but Z5 remains low (5%), suggesting untapped VO2 max stimulus potential.

insights.title: Cadence variability linked to fatigue and pace
insights.body: Cadence ranged from 87 spm (April 26, 14:00 min/km, HR 120) to 150 spm (April 22, 7:13 min/km, HR 143), with recent runs showing tighter clustering (146–150 spm) at sub-9 min/km paces — indicating form stability improves with consistent effort below fatigue threshold.

insights.title: Reduced high-intensity load but elevated aerobic TE
insights.body: Although Z4 time increased (+5 pts), total high-intensity (Z4+Z5) time is only 22% this month vs 13% last month — yet aerobic TE rose +0.2. This suggests your Z4 efforts (e.g., April 12: 5.0 km @ 7:42 min/km, HR 163) are exceptionally productive for aerobic development.

recommendations.action: Do a 4.5 km Zone 2 run (HR 125–135 bpm) on one of the remaining 3 days, maintaining cadence ≥145 spm and stride length ≥85 cm (based on your efficient 7:13–7:42 runs)
recommendations.reason: Your Z1/Z2 foundation strengthened (23% Z1), but sustained Zone 2 volume remains moderate — this session will reinforce aerobic efficiency gains without adding fatigue.

recommendations.action: Insert a 6-min progressive surge within your next easy run: start at 9:00 min/km (HR ~125), build every 2 min to 7:30 min/km (HR ~155), holding cadence ≥146 spm throughout
recommendations.reason: Your April 12 and April 22 runs show strong efficiency at 7:13–7:42 min/km with cadence 146–150; this drill bridges easy and threshold efforts while preserving form.

recommendations.action: After your next run >4 km, perform 3 × 1-min strides at 6:00–6:15 min/km (HR ~165–170), focusing on ground contact time ≤300 ms (you hit 298 ms on April 22)
recommendations.reason: Your best ground contact time (298 ms) occurred during a fast 3.1 km run — short strides will reinforce neuromuscular efficiency without overstressing recovery.

weekly_focus.description: Strengthen the connection between heart rate control, cadence consistency, and ground contact time to lock in aerobic gains — using pace as a secondary cue, not the primary driver.
suggested_sessions: 5 km mixed-effort run with 6-min progressive surge
